skill.name: elixir-pro
skill.description: Write idiomatic Elixir code with OTP patterns, supervision trees, and Phoenix LiveView. Masters concurrency, fault tolerance, and distributed systems.
skill.summary: Create idiomatic Elixir, OTP, Phoenix, and LiveView guidance for reliable systems.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a false positive caused by Markdown backticks around a resource path in SKILL.md. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or unsafe execution instructions were found in the reviewed file.

static_findings.snippet: - If detailed examples are required, open `resources/implementation-playbook.md`.

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md line 24 uses Markdown backticks to format the path resources/implementation-playbook.md. It does not instruct the agent to execute shell commands or interpolate user input.

content.value_statement: Elixir teams need guidance for OTP, Phoenix, concurrency, and fault-tolerant design. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code produce idiomatic plans, reviews, tests, and architecture advice.
actual_capabilities: Plans OTP supervision trees and application boundaries.
Reviews Elixir and Phoenix code for idioms and maintainability.
Suggests GenServer, Task, and process design patterns.
Recommends Ecto changeset and context organization practices.
Outlines ExUnit, doctest, and property-based testing strategies.
Identifies BEAM profiling, telemetry, and performance review steps.
limitations: It does not run Mix commands or verify results without tool access.
It needs project context to give precise Phoenix or OTP recommendations.
It cannot prove distributed behavior without tests and runtime evidence.
It does not replace production review for security or reliability decisions.

use_cases.title: Design an OTP Service
use_cases.description: Create a supervision approach for a new service with restart strategy, process ownership, and failure boundaries.

use_cases.title: Improve Phoenix Contexts
use_cases.description: Review context boundaries, Ecto changesets, and LiveView update flows for a growing Phoenix application.

use_cases.title: Plan Reliability Reviews
use_cases.description: Prepare a checklist for observability, testing, profiling, and fault handling before a release.

prompt_templates.title: Review Basic Elixir Code
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Elixir module for idiomatic naming, pattern matching, guard usage, and simple ExUnit coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Phoenix Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a Phoenix feature with contexts, Ecto changesets, LiveView state, and tests. Ask for missing domain details first.

prompt_templates.title: Design OTP Supervision
prompt_templates.prompt: Propose an OTP supervision tree for this service. Include process responsibilities, restart strategy, failure modes, and telemetry points.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Distributed Elixir
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this distributed Elixir architecture for clustering risks, back pressure, process isolation, observability, and deployment validation.

output_examples.input: Review a GenServer that stores user session state.
output_examples.output: A focused review covering state ownership, call and cast boundaries, restart behavior, timeout handling, and test scenarios.

output_examples.input: Plan a LiveView dashboard backed by Ecto data.
output_examples.output: A structured plan for contexts, changesets, data loading, PubSub updates, LiveView assigns, and ExUnit coverage.

output_examples.input: Prepare a BEAM performance checklist before launch.
output_examples.output: A checklist covering telemetry events, observer and recon profiling, queue length checks, memory review, and benchmark targets.

best_practices: Provide project context, framework versions, and the current failure mode.
Ask for supervision, testing, and telemetry guidance together for OTP work.
Validate recommendations with ExUnit, Dialyzer, profiling, and staged deployment checks.
anti_patterns: Do not request broad rewrites without explaining the current architecture.
Do not apply OTP patterns when a simple function or module is enough.
Do not treat generated guidance as verified runtime behavior.

faq.question: Can this skill write Elixir code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can help draft idiomatic Elixir modules, OTP designs, Phoenix changes, and related tests.

faq.question: Does it support Phoenix LiveView?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for LiveView state, real-time updates, contexts, and testing patterns.

faq.question: Can it debug production incidents?
faq.answer: It can help structure investigation steps, but it needs logs, metrics, traces, and runtime details.

faq.question: Does it execute Mix tasks?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance unless the host tool has explicit command execution access.

faq.question: Is it useful for distributed Elixir?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review clustering, process isolation, back pressure, supervision, and observability concerns.

faq.question: What should I include in prompts?
faq.answer: Include code snippets, goals, versions, known constraints, expected behavior, and current errors.
